Situation:   Lovers caught on opposite sides of a global confict.
Sentence:    Ex-Fighter Pilot, Archibald Stone (Arch) battles his heart and mind torn by his fiance.
Paragraph:   Soon after retiring from the USAF, Arch accepts help from his fiance to land a civilian job in Weapons manufacturing. Jessica Mallory (Jessie) is a lobbyist and registered agent for Egypt and has deep connections inside Washington DC, particularly the Pentagon. Together, Arch and Jessie slowly uncover each others secrets, putting their loyalty for each other against their loyalties for their principles.
Page:        Arch's nerves were tested beyond the brink of breaking during what would be his final mission. Against United States adversaries in the Middle-East, he witnessed the diabolical use of new weapons that took his entire squadron out, escaping the same fate through a quirk. 
             
             After a decision to retire, Arch reunites with Jess, his fiance, in Washington DC, where they rekindle their romance, like so many times he has returned from a tour. Unlike those times, he faces a civilian life and begins to struggle with the unstructured and messy nature of freedom of obligations to his command. Rather than sit idly, Arch takes Jess up on an offer to work with one of her connections in the Weapons industry.
             
             Soon after joining the ranks of civilian life, working in Sales for Advanscion Aerospace, coincidences build a fact pattern that connects his prior life in the AF with his new life. The weapons he saw in use in the skies were a product being sold to the highest bidder and the people working closest to him may have had a hand in deleting his squadron. The new class of weapons stir conflict inside Arch, as their capabilities are indefensible, terrifying, and inhumane. The characters involved in the design, sale, and use of the weapons land on a spectrum of morally conscious to morally void.
             
             The coincidences don't end with his civilian business dealings, they hit home. As things at work grow increasingly uncomfortable, Arch suspects Jessie knows more than she has been letting on. All the signs were there at the beginning, but her motivations are complex. Complex enough to send Arch into a moral crisis.
             
             In the end, does Arch side with the Red, White, and Blue; or can Jessie sway his loyalties to see things her way?
